overview: Carnewas is the National Trust clifftop above Bedruthan, between Newquay and Padstow, and it’s where you come for one of the classic views of the north coast: a line of giant rock stacks marching along the beach far below. It’s an easy place to stop, with a car park, shop and tea room right by the viewpoints.
One important thing to know: you can’t get down to Bedruthan beach. Cliff falls damaged the staircase in 2019, and it remains closed with no safe alternative route, so enjoy the view from the top.

expect.title: The view
expect.text: Short paths from the car park lead to viewpoints looking down on the stacks, with the coast stretching away towards Trevose Head.

expect.title: Clifftop walks
expect.text: About three-quarters of a mile of the South West Coast Path runs through the site, so you can easily stretch it into a longer walk.

expect.title: Tea room and shop
expect.text: The tea room (not run by the Trust) sells drinks and food, and there’s a gift shop with local products, plus picnic tables on the grass.

goodToKnow.label: The beach is closed
goodToKnow.text: The stairs to Bedruthan beach have been closed since a rock fall in 2019. Don’t try to find another way down: the cliffs are unstable, the currents are strong and you could be cut off by the tide.

goodToKnow.label: Parking
goodToKnow.text: Pay and display for most visitors; parking is free if you’re a National Trust member or have a Blue Badge. The machines need exact change in coins, or use the parking app, ideally downloaded before you arrive as signal is patchy.

goodToKnow.label: Dogs
goodToKnow.text: Welcome under close control, especially near livestock and the cliff edges, and on leads in the tea-room garden.

goodToKnow.label: Opening
goodToKnow.text: The clifftop is open dawn to dusk; check winter opening for the tea room.

week.text: A quick, rewarding stop on a drive along the coast between Newquay and Padstow, ideally on a clear day for the view. Combine it with a beach at Mawgan Porth just down the road.

pairWith.why: a sandy family beach just down the coast
a little cove village to the north

tips: Come late in the afternoon for the light on the stacks.
Bring coins or download the parking app before you go: mobile signal is patchy.
